description:
Why SpaceX’s Mars timeline is more radical than it sounds.

SpaceX wants to land an uncrewed Starship on Mars as early as 2026.

That timeline isn’t just ambitious, it’s constrained by physics.
The Earth, Mars launch window only opens every 26 months, turning what sounds like a vision into a hard deadline.

But this plan depends on Starship V3, which requires breakthroughs in thermal protection, propulsion efficiency, and orbital refueling all at a scale never demonstrated before.

This isn’t a mission yet.
It’s a stress test of whether impossible milestones can be compressed into a single launch window.

title: Why SpaceX’s Mars plan is on a clock
